policy: Only conflicting established simulator values are findings; an unknown beside a value is an evidence gap, not a disagreement.
The authentic baseline remains separate from every simulator observation and is never rewritten by majority vote.
Supported departure means the curated baseline has high-confidence manufacturer or homologation evidence; it does not infer why a simulator differs.
Provisional departure means the simulator conflict is real but the authentic baseline needs stronger independent evidence before publication as a benchmark verdict.

findings.display_name: Audi R8 LMS GT3 Evo II

authentic_baseline.basis: Audi's exact 2022-car technical data establishes the electrohydraulically operated racing clutch, and a first-person test of the exact Evo II directly describes using its steering-wheel-mounted clutch lever to move off. Together they establish a driver-operated hand clutch for the standing start; neither source establishes a pedal, anti-stall, or automated launch procedure.

authentic_baseline.basis: The existing curated record already established a display-free wheel rim from a live AMS2 cockpit inspection; the AC guided drive's independent cockpit observation of the same real car agrees. No manufacturer or period documentation for a factory-fitted display was found, consistent with a 1971-1973 production car. Both the existing curated record's live-cockpit finding and the AC guided drive's independent cockpit observation agree on a closed (non-open-top) rim; no contrary period documentation was found. Two independent simulator recreations of the same real car agree on a round wheel rim, consistent with the existing curated record's live-cockpit finding. Neither cockpit observation shows rim-mounted shift lights, consistent with a 1971-1973 road car predating such systems; agrees with the existing curated record. No period Miura electronics package included automatic throttle blipping; the existing curated record already established this for the same real car, and the reviewed manufacturer history describes no such system. Carried forward from the existing curated record; a 1971-1973 road car has no automatic ignition or throttle-cut system, and the field is not applicable to downshifts under the database's own convention. The Miura's synchronised five-speed manual supports clutchless running downshifts as ordinary technique; this matches the existing curated record's already-established value. The real-car value is carried forward unchanged from the existing curated record: a synchronised gearbox eases with a downshift blip but does not require it to engage the gear. The AC guided drive's two-stage test found the exact AC 14923034 implementation requires a manual blip to accept a repeated downshift; that stricter behavior is recorded separately as a simulator override on the observation, not as a change to the authentic real-car value, matching the project's existing AC BMW 3.0 CSL / Ford GT40 Mk I precedent. Carried forward from the existing curated record; throttle-lift is an upshift concern under the database's convention and is not applicable to downshifts. Both the manufacturer's official history and an independent secondary technical profile state a five-speed manual transmission for the Miura P400 SV, matching the existing curated record. No reviewed source explicitly states synchromesh construction; this is carried forward at the same medium confidence as the existing curated record, which itself treats synchromesh as the ordinary reading of a period road-car manual gearbox rather than a stated specification. The manufacturer source and the existing curated record agree on a conventional H-pattern manual shifter; no sequential or paddle system exists on this period road car. Two independent simulators' direct gear-selection testing (AMS2 in the existing curated record and this AC guided drive) both report a standard, non-dogleg H pattern for the same real car. The manufacturer source documents a clutch-equipped five-speed manual across the Miura family; a manual clutch is required from rest, matching the existing curated record. Carried forward from the existing curated record; automatic blipping does not apply to upshifts. No period Miura electronics package included an automatic shift-cut system; matches the existing curated record. The synchronised five-speed manual supports clutchless running upshifts with a throttle lift as ordinary technique, matching the existing curated record. Carried forward from the existing curated record; manual blipping does not apply to upshifts. A clutchless running upshift on this synchronised gearbox requires a throttle lift to unload the drivetrain, matching the existing curated record.

authentic_baseline.basis: The official technical sheet specifies six forward ratios and contemporary coverage confirms a six-speed automatic. The manufacturer sheet explicitly says automatic and specifies a torque converter; Quatro Rodas corroborates the automatic 200 TSI configuration. The launch equipment list and contemporary coverage document steering-wheel paddles for the automatic Virtus 200 TSI. The sources explicitly describe sequential changes using the automatic transmission's steering-wheel paddles. The exact 200 TSI Virtus uses an automatic torque-converter transmission; normal move-off is performed through the automatic selector, brake, and accelerator without driver clutch operation. Paddle upshifts operate the automatic transmission; the documented driver interface has no clutch operation. Paddle downshifts operate the automatic transmission; the documented driver interface has no clutch operation. The exact car has an automatic Tiptronic/paddle interface rather than a manual gearbox requiring a driver throttle blip on upshift. The exact car has an automatic Tiptronic/paddle interface rather than a manual gearbox requiring a driver throttle blip on downshift. The full-resolution 2018 Virtus Highline cockpit photograph shows a conventional continuous rim with a clearly flattened lower section, not fixed GT/formula grips. The photograph shows the digital instrument cluster behind the rim, and the written source places the display in the separate cluster rather than in the wheel. The full-resolution image shows the upper band of the conventional wheel intact; only the lower section is flattened. The clear cockpit photograph shows no dedicated shift/rev-light strip on the rim; the visible digital display is separate behind it. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
